forms.pageTitle: How to Prepare for Umrah from Pakistan: Complete 12-Step Checklist (2026)
forms.pageSeoDescription: Step-by-step Umrah preparation checklist for Pakistani pilgrims — passport, vaccinations, Saudi visa, hotel proximity, Ihram, packing, flights, transport, and pre-departure final checks.
forms.pageBody:
Most pilgrims focus only on picking a package and paying the deposit, then scramble in the final week trying to remember everything else. The result is predictable: missing documents at Jeddah immigration, a forgotten polio booster, a hotel that turns out to be 900 metres from the Haram, or Ihram bought at the airport in a panic. This checklist is the one we walk every Pakistani pilgrim through before they board the plane — built from what actually goes wrong, not what looks good on a brochure.

Whether you are performing Umrah for the first time, taking your parents in their seventies, travelling as a mosque group of forty, or doing a solo two-week Ramadan trip, the same twelve preparation steps apply. Skip any of them and you risk delays, fidya penalties, or a Saudi-side scramble. Use this page as your live checklist from the day you start planning to the morning of your flight.

Why preparation matters more than the package itself

Umrah is two things at once: a profound act of worship and an international journey with real logistics — visas, vaccinations, currency, customs, airline baggage rules, hotel check-ins, ground transport between Madinah and Makkah, and the Saudi state's growing use of the Nusuk app for permits. The pilgrims who travel calmly and focus on ibadah are the ones who prepared properly. The pilgrims who spend the first two days panicking at the front desk are the ones who treated Umrah like a leisure trip and were surprised when it wasn't.

Proper preparation lets you arrive with documents in order, no missing vaccinations, hotel keys ready, Ihram pre-fitted, family members briefed on what to do at the Miqat, and your spiritual focus intact from the moment you cross Qarn al-Manazil. The rest of this guide walks through the twelve steps in the order our own group leaders work them.

Step 1 — Choose the right Umrah package tier and dates

The single biggest decision is when you go and what tier you pick. Both affect price by 2–4x.

Cheapest months for Umrah from Pakistan are November and February — package costs PKR 235,000–290,000 per person for an economy 14-day trip. Ramadan packages (especially the last 10 nights) can hit PKR 700,000+ for the same trip. Hotel proximity is the single biggest tier driver: a 3-star at 500m+ from the Haram is half the price of a 4-star at 200m, but the 500m walk in 38°C heat will exhaust elderly pilgrims.

Before signing any deposit, confirm the exact hotel name (not just the star rating), how many metres from the Haram, how many pilgrims per room (most Pakistani packages assume triple/quad sharing), and whether transport from Pakistani airport to Saudi hotel is included on both ends. See our full family Umrah packages guide for tier-by-tier pricing breakdowns.

Step 2 — Verify passport and document validity 90 days before departure

Your Pakistani Machine-Readable Passport must be valid for at least six months beyond your intended return date. If yours is borderline, renew at any DGI&P Passport Office (PKR 4,500 standard MRP, 21 working days). Do not wait until the last month — Saudi authorities reject visa applications where passport expiry is too close.

Documents you need ready: original MRP passport, CNIC (front and back copies), two recent passport-size photographs (white background, 4×6 cm, no glasses), confirmed return ticket, and confirmed hotel booking. Photocopies should be kept in a separate bag — a lost original at Jeddah airport without backup copies has cost more than one pilgrim a full day of immigration delays.

Step 3 — Get vaccinations early (do not leave to the last week)

Two vaccinations are mandatory for every Pakistani Umrah traveller and both have timing rules:

  • Polio booster — must be administered between 28 days and 12 months before arrival in Saudi. Free at any government EPI centre in Pakistan. The yellow vaccination card is physically checked at Jeddah and Madinah immigration. Do not get the booster on the day before your flight — the 28-day minimum disqualifies it.
  • Meningococcal ACWY — required, valid for 3 years. Available at private hospitals for PKR 4,000–6,500 (Aga Khan, Doctors Hospital, Hameed Latif, South City, Northwest General).

Bring both vaccination certificates with you — Saudi airport immigration is increasingly strict on physical proof.

Step 4 — Confirm which Saudi visa route applies to you

You have three Saudi Umrah visa options. Pick one and stick to it:

  1. Traditional MoFA Umrah Visa via Pakistani agent — bundled into most package prices, processed in 5–14 days, single entry, 30-day stay, 90-day visa validity.
  2. Nusuk Masar e-Visa (self-apply) — direct online at nusuk.sa, processed in 24–72 hours, SAR 535 (~PKR 39,000), same single-entry/30-day rules.
  3. Saudi Tourist e-Visa — allows Umrah AND tourism (Riyadh, AlUla, etc), multi-entry, 1-year validity, 90-day stay. Pakistanis currently apply via Saudi embassy in Islamabad / consulate in Karachi, USD 137.

Most Pakistani families use route 1 (via agent) because the package handles all the visa logistics. Solo travellers or experienced pilgrims often use route 2. Frequent business travellers or those combining Umrah with Riyadh visits use route 3. See our Saudi e-Visa guide and Umrah Visa vs Tourist Visa comparison for full detail.

Step 5 — Lock down flights and hotel proximity

Flights and hotels are 60% of total Umrah cost. Confirm:

  • Departure airport (Lahore, Karachi, Islamabad — see Umrah from Lahore and Umrah from Karachi guides for connectivity options)
  • Airline (PIA, Saudia, Air Sial, FlyJinnah — see airline comparison)
  • Direct or transit (transit via Dubai/Doha adds 3–5 hours total)
  • Baggage allowance (30 kg + 7 kg cabin is standard on full-service; 20 kg base on FlyJinnah)
  • Madinah-first or Jeddah-first itinerary
  • Hotel name in Makkah AND distance to Haram in metres (under 400m is the comfort threshold for families)
  • Hotel name in Madinah AND distance to Masjid al-Nabawi
  • Room sharing arrangement (triple/quad standard for Pakistani packages)

Step 6 — Learn the Umrah rites before you fly

Every first-time pilgrim should arrive in Saudi already knowing what Tawaf, Sa'i, Halq, and Tahallul mean — not learning them at the Miqat. The four core rites are:

  1. Enter Ihram at the Miqat (Qarn al-Manazil if flying to Jeddah, or Bir Ali if going via Madinah)
  2. Make Niyyah and Talbiyah — declare intention and recite the Talbiyah
  3. Tawaf — 7 anti-clockwise laps of the Kaabah (≈1 km)
  4. Sa'i — 7 trips between Safa and Marwah (≈3.5 km)
  5. Halq or Taqsir — men shave (preferred) or trim; women trim a fingertip's length

Read our first-time Umrah guide in advance. Attend any pre-departure briefing your agent offers — most Pakistani operators host one 2–3 days before flight, often at a community centre or mosque.

Step 7 — Prepare your Ihram properly

Men: bring two sets of Ihram cloth (one to wear, one spare), an Ihram belt with a zipped pocket for documents, and plastic Ihram slippers with no stitching across the top. Buy from any Pakistani Umrah supply shop or at the international departure lounge of Lahore, Karachi, or Islamabad airports.

Women: pack 3–4 loose breathable cotton abayas, prayer scarves, and comfortable closed-toe walking shoes (not flip-flops — Masjid al-Haram floors get scorching).

Once in Ihram, you cannot cut nails, cut hair, apply perfume or scented products, cover the head (men), use stitched clothing (men), or marry. Pack unscented soap, unscented toothpaste (Sensodyne Original works), and unscented deodorant for the Ihram period. Save scented items for after Halq.

Step 8 — Pack smart, not heavy

Pakistani airlines on the Saudi route allow 30 kg checked + 7 kg cabin. The temptation is to fill every gram — resist it. Buses in Saudi have limited under-deck space, hotel elevators get packed during check-in, and you will be hauling your own bag at multiple points. Our full Umrah packing checklist covers exactly what to bring, but the essentials in priority order are: documents (carry-on, never checked), Ihram, prayer essentials, comfortable walking shoes, basic medicines, unscented toiletries, universal adapter (Saudi uses Type G UK 3-pin), and a power bank under 10,000 mAh.

Step 9 — Build a health and emergency kit

Personal medical preparation is non-negotiable for elderly pilgrims, those with chronic conditions, or anyone over 60. Bring:

  • Personal prescription medicines in original packaging plus a doctor's note (Saudi customs occasionally checks)
  • Panadol / Paracetamol (you will walk 5–10 km per day, sometimes more)
  • Strepsils for sore throats (Saudi AC + dust is the #1 health complaint)
  • Imodium and oral rehydration salts (ORS sachets)
  • Blister plasters, antiseptic cream, basic wound dressing
  • N95 or surgical masks for tawaf crowds and during flu season
  • SPF 50+ sunblock (allowed in Ihram only if odorless)

Save these emergency contacts on your phone before departure: Pakistani Embassy Riyadh, Pakistani Consulate Jeddah, your Pakistani group leader's mobile, your hotel address in Arabic (for taxis), and your insurance provider's 24-hour line.

Step 10 — Confirm transport, ziyarat, and Saudi logistics

A complete Pakistani Umrah package should include airport pickup at Jeddah or Madinah, ground transport between Madinah and Makkah (4.5 hours by bus), Saudi-side hotel transfers, ziyarat tours in both cities, and airport drop-off on return. Confirm in writing — not verbally — which of these are bundled. "Transport included" sometimes means only Saudi-side transport, leaving the Pakistani airport transfer for you to arrange.

Download the Nusuk app before you fly. Many Saudi ground services now require it — Riyadul Jannah reservations, Rawda visit slots, occasionally Tawaf permits in peak season. Also download Tawakkalna (health declarations) and Google Maps with offline copies of both Makkah and Madinah city maps.

Step 11 — Plan for family pilgrims (children, elderly, special needs)

Family Umrah requires extra thought:

  • Children's vaccinations and passports must be processed individually — even infants need a Saudi visa
  • Wheelchair rentals at the Haram cost SAR 100–200 (with deposit)
  • Dedicated wheelchair Tawaf tracks exist on the second and third floor; Sa'i can also be performed in wheelchair
  • Hotel proximity matters more for families — pick something under 400m even if it costs more
  • Quad rooms book out fastest, especially for Ramadan and December — reserve 3+ months ahead
  • Pack familiar snacks and small entertainment for children's hotel-room downtime

Step 12 — Run a final pre-departure check 48 hours before flight

The morning of your flight is too late to discover a missing document. Run this final check 48 hours before departure:

  • All documents printed (passport, Saudi e-Visa printout, vaccination card, hotel vouchers, return ticket) — kept in carry-on
  • Digital copies of all documents emailed to yourself
  • Group leader's mobile saved + tested via WhatsApp
  • SAR cash exchanged (use Anarkali/Mall Road in Lahore, Saddar/Tariq Road in Karachi, NOT airport)
  • Saudi SIM card plan decided (buy on arrival at Jeddah for SAR 70–120 with data, or activate international roaming)
  • Nail-cutting, hair trim, and shower done the night before (Sunnah of Ihram preparation)
  • Ihram packed and accessible without unpacking
  • Boarding pass on phone AND printed
  • Polio + meningococcal cards in the same folder as passport

Common mistakes Pakistani pilgrims make

  • Booking the cheapest package without confirming the exact hotel and distance from Haram
  • Getting the polio booster less than 28 days before departure (disqualifies it)
  • Bringing scented soap or scented toiletries for the Ihram period
  • Underestimating the Madinah-to-Makkah journey time (5 hours minimum including check-in and Miqat stop)
  • Carrying ZamZam in personal luggage instead of using the airline's free 5L allowance
  • Arriving at Pakistani airport less than 4 hours before international departure during peak Umrah season
  • Not memorising the Miqat — entering Ihram after crossing it requires fidya
  • Assuming Tawaf and Sa'i are short — they total ~4.5 km of walking
  • Skipping the pre-departure briefing

Working with Al Bari Travel & Tours

Al Bari Travel runs as a remote-first agency through named Regional Representatives across Pakistan and the USA. Every booking is handled end-to-end by a named human — no call centres, no bots, no fuss. Our group leaders have personally accompanied over 40 Umrah departures each, and most of the checklist above came from problems we solved on the ground in Madinah and Makkah. Quotations within 4 hours during Pakistan business hours.

pageFaqs.q: When should I start preparing for Umrah from Pakistan?
pageFaqs.a: Start 90 days before your intended departure date. Passport renewal (if needed) takes 21 working days, vaccinations need to be timed properly (polio booster between 28 days and 12 months before arrival), Saudi visa processing is 5–14 days, and Pakistani agent package bookings often have a 60-day cancellation deadline. Starting 3 months ahead gives comfortable buffer.

pageFaqs.q: What is the minimum passport validity for Umrah from Pakistan?
pageFaqs.a: Saudi authorities require your Pakistani passport to be valid for at least 6 months beyond your intended departure from Saudi Arabia. If your passport expires within 9 months of your planned return, renew before you book.

pageFaqs.q: Are both polio and meningococcal vaccines mandatory for Pakistani Umrah pilgrims?
pageFaqs.a: Yes. The polio booster (valid 28 days to 12 months before arrival) is free at any Pakistani EPI centre and is checked at Saudi immigration. The meningococcal ACWY vaccine is valid for 3 years and costs PKR 4,000–6,500 at private hospitals. Both yellow cards must be carried physically — Saudi immigration does ask for them.

pageFaqs.q: How much does an economy Umrah package from Pakistan cost in 2026?
pageFaqs.a: Economy 14-day Umrah packages from Pakistan range from PKR 235,000 to 290,000 per person (3-star hotels, 500m+ from Haram). Standard tier (4-star, 200–400m) is PKR 335,000 to 410,000. Premium tier (5-star, within 200m) is PKR 510,000+. Ramadan, December school break, and Hajj-adjacent months can be 50–100% more expensive.

pageFaqs.q: What hotel distance from Masjid al-Haram is acceptable for elderly pilgrims?
pageFaqs.a: Within 200–300m is comfortable for elderly pilgrims; under 400m is the upper limit for most families. Beyond 500m, the walk in summer heat becomes exhausting and requires return-trip rest between prayers. Premium 5-star options like Ajyad and Misfalah hotels sit within 200m. Confirm exact distance before booking — "near the Haram" can mean anything from 100m to 1.5km.

pageFaqs.q: Do I need to learn Umrah rituals before travelling?
pageFaqs.a: Strongly recommended. First-time pilgrims who arrive without knowing what Tawaf, Sa'i, Halq, and Niyyah mean often miss small but important details (like reciting the Talbiyah audibly, or running between the two green markers during Sa'i — which is for men only). Most Pakistani Umrah operators host a pre-departure briefing 2–3 days before flight; attend it.

pageFaqs.q: Can I prepare for Umrah from Pakistan without using an agent?
pageFaqs.a: Yes — book the Saudi Umrah visa directly via Nusuk Masar (nusuk.sa), book your own flights and hotels, and arrange Saudi-side transport on arrival. It saves money but requires significantly more research. Most first-time pilgrims and families use a Pakistani agent for the convenience and ground support. Experienced pilgrims and solo travellers often self-book.

pageFaqs.q: What if I forget something — can I buy it in Saudi Arabia?
pageFaqs.a: Most items (Ihram, unscented toiletries, prayer mats, dates) are widely available in Saudi at souqs around the Haram. The exceptions are your personal prescription medicines (often unavailable or under different brand names) and any specific Pakistani brands you depend on. Prioritise medicines and documents — everything else is replaceable.

forms.pageTitle: Mahram Affidavit for Pakistani Women Performing Hajj or Umrah (2026)
forms.pageSeoTitle: Mahram Affidavit Template Pakistan — Hajj & Umrah Women
forms.pageSeoDescription: Mahram affidavit guide for Pakistani women under 45 performing Hajj or Umrah — stamp paper, format, Oath Commissioner, what to include, common pitfalls.
forms.pageBody:
The mahram affidavit is one of the most-asked-about documents in the Pakistani Hajj / Umrah pipeline. Pakistani women under 45 travelling for pilgrimage with a male relative (father, brother, husband, son) typically need a notarised affidavit documenting that relationship, the joint travel dates, and the joint accommodation arrangements. This page explains what the affidavit must contain, how to prepare it, and the rules as they stand in 2026.

Who needs a mahram affidavit?

Saudi Arabia relaxed the mahram requirement in 2021, permitting women aged 45+ to perform Hajj or Umrah without a mahram in supervised groups. For women under 45, the mahram requirement is still enforced by:

  • The Pakistan Government Hajj Scheme (strict)
  • Most private Pakistani Hajj Group Operators (HGOs) — some have additional flexibility, especially for adult sisters travelling together
  • Saudi MoFA when processing certain visa categories

The affidavit is the formal proof that the male traveller is genuinely a mahram under Islamic and Pakistani legal definitions.

What the affidavit must contain

  1. Full legal names of the woman and the mahram, with CNIC numbers
  2. The exact nature of the mahram relationship (father / brother / husband / son)
  3. Statement that they will travel together, share accommodation appropriately, and the mahram will be responsible for the woman's wellbeing throughout the journey
  4. Specific Hajj or Umrah travel dates (departure and return)
  5. Statement that the affidavit is being executed voluntarily, in full awareness of its contents
  6. Signatures of both parties + signatures of two witnesses (with their CNIC numbers)
  7. Date and place of execution
  8. Stamp of the Oath Commissioner (notary)

How to execute the affidavit

  1. Draft the affidavit (use a standard template — many lawyers and stamp paper vendors provide one)
  2. Print on Rs. 50 (PKR 50) stamp paper purchased from the relevant Treasury or stamp vendor
  3. Both parties sign in front of the Oath Commissioner
  4. Oath Commissioner stamps and registers the affidavit (cost approximately PKR 200-500 in 2026)
  5. Retain the original; make at least 3 photocopies (one for the Hajj operator, one for the Saudi-side Mu'allim, one for personal records)

Marriage certificate or birth certificate is also required

The affidavit alone is not enough. You also need documentary proof of the mahram relationship:

  • Husband-wife: Original NADRA Computerised Marriage Certificate (NOT just the original Nikah-nama)
  • Father-daughter or brother-sister: NADRA Family Registration Certificate (FRC) or both parties' B-Form showing same father
  • Mother-son: Same — FRC or B-Form

Submit photocopies of both the affidavit and the relationship document with the Hajj / Umrah file.

Common pitfalls Pakistani women face

  • Submitting only the affidavit without the supporting NADRA documents (file rejected)
  • Submitting the original Nikah-nama without the NADRA Computerised Marriage Certificate (Saudi authorities require the latter)
  • Affidavit signed but not notarised by an Oath Commissioner (invalid)
  • Stamp paper missing or expired stamp duty (invalid)
  • Witnesses without CNIC numbers or signatures (invalid)
  • Trying to use a non-mahram (cousin, brother-in-law, uncle) — Saudi rules are strict on mahram definitions

What if no mahram is available?

For Hajj specifically, women aged 45+ can travel in officially supervised groups without a mahram (Saudi rule since 2021). Some private Pakistani Hajj operators have established women-only groups under qualified female group leaders for this category. For Umrah, the same 45+ supervised-group rule applies. Women under 45 without a mahram should:

  1. Consider waiting until a male family relative can accompany them
  2. Explore private operators with established women-only supervised group options for 45+
  3. Consult a qualified Islamic scholar for guidance specific to their circumstance

Al Bari Travel handles mahram affidavit coordination and supporting documentation as part of our standard Umrah and Hajj package services for Pakistani families. WhatsApp +92 315 9596161 for a free consultation.

pageFaqs.q: Is a mahram affidavit required for women over 45?
pageFaqs.a: No. Since 2021, Saudi Arabia permits women aged 45 and above to travel for Hajj and Umrah without a mahram, provided they travel in officially supervised groups. Some private Pakistani Hajj operators have established women-only groups for this category.

pageFaqs.q: Can a brother-in-law or cousin serve as a mahram?
pageFaqs.a: No. Under Islamic and Pakistani legal definitions used by Saudi authorities, mahram is restricted to specific male relatives: father, son, brother, husband, paternal grandfather, maternal grandfather, paternal uncle (in some interpretations), maternal uncle (in some interpretations), step-father (after marriage consummation), nephew. Cousins and brothers-in-law are NOT mahrams.

pageFaqs.q: How much does the mahram affidavit cost to prepare?
pageFaqs.a: The Rs. 50 stamp paper itself is PKR 50. The Oath Commissioner's fee is typically PKR 200-500. Templates from lawyers or stamp paper vendors may add PKR 500-1,500. Total cost is usually under PKR 2,000.

pageFaqs.q: Do I need a separate affidavit for each pilgrimage?
pageFaqs.a: Yes. The affidavit must specify the exact dates of THIS Hajj or Umrah journey. If you return to Saudi later for a different Umrah, a fresh affidavit is needed for the new dates.

pageFaqs.q: Can the affidavit be in English or must it be Urdu?
pageFaqs.a: English is preferred by Saudi authorities and by most Pakistani Hajj operators. Urdu is accepted but may require a certified English translation. Bilingual (English + Urdu) is fine and often the safest choice.

pageFaqs.q: What if my Pakistani Hajj operator says no affidavit is needed?
pageFaqs.a: Some private operators bundle the affidavit preparation into their service. Confirm in writing whether they handle it or expect you to provide it. The Pakistan Government Hajj Scheme strictly requires you to provide a notarised affidavit yourself.

forms.pageTitle: Polio Vaccination Card for Pakistani Travellers to Saudi Arabia (2026)
forms.pageSeoTitle: Polio Vaccination for Saudi Travel from Pakistan — Yellow Card
forms.pageSeoDescription: How Pakistani travellers get the mandatory polio booster for Saudi Arabia entry — free EPI centres, timing rules (28 days to 12 months before arrival), yellow card.
forms.pageBody:
Saudi Arabia requires every Pakistani traveller to show proof of a recent polio vaccination booster on arrival at Jeddah or Madinah immigration. This requirement applies to ALL Pakistani nationals regardless of visa type (Umrah, Hajj, Tourist, Work, Family). Without the yellow vaccination card, you can be denied entry or detained at the airport. This guide explains everything about getting the booster correctly.

Why polio vaccination is mandatory

Pakistan is one of only two countries (along with Afghanistan) where wild poliovirus is still considered endemic by the WHO. To protect global pilgrim populations — Saudi Arabia hosts over 2 million Hajj and 6+ million Umrah pilgrims annually — Saudi MoFA has required polio vaccination for Pakistani travellers since 2014. The rule is strictly enforced at airport immigration.

Critical timing rule

The polio booster MUST be administered:

  • Minimum 28 days before your scheduled arrival in Saudi Arabia (so the immune response has time to develop)
  • Maximum 12 months before your scheduled arrival (otherwise it's considered expired)

If you get the booster less than 28 days before flight, Saudi immigration will reject the card as invalid. If you got one more than 12 months ago, you need a fresh one.

Where to get the booster in Pakistan (FREE)

The polio booster is FREE for all Pakistani citizens at any government EPI (Expanded Programme on Immunization) centre. Major centres:

Punjab

  • District Health Office in every city + town
  • Government hospitals (Mayo, Services, Holy Family, Allied, DHQ in each district)
  • Designated EPI centres in every Tehsil

Sindh

  • Civil Hospital, Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre, Sindh Government Hospitals (Karachi)
  • Liaquat University Hospital (Hyderabad)
  • Chandka Medical College Hospital (Larkana)

Khyber Pakhtunkhwa

  • Khyber Teaching Hospital, Lady Reading Hospital (Peshawar)
  • District Headquarters Hospitals in every district

Balochistan

  • Civil Hospital Quetta, Bolan Medical Complex

ICT (Islamabad / Rawalpindi)

  • Polyclinic Hospital Islamabad, Holy Family Hospital Rawalpindi, all District Health Offices

What to bring

  • Original CNIC (or B-Form for minors)
  • Original passport (so the vaccination card matches your passport name)
  • Photocopy of CNIC and passport bio page

What the yellow card looks like

The official polio vaccination certificate is a small yellow booklet (or sometimes a single yellow card) issued by the EPI clinic. It contains:

  • Your full name (matching passport)
  • Passport number
  • Date of vaccination
  • Vaccine batch number
  • Vaccinator's signature + clinic stamp
  • WHO official stamp

Keep the original card with your passport. Photocopies are NOT accepted at Saudi immigration.

What if you lose your yellow card?

You cannot replace it — you'll need to get the booster again at any EPI centre and receive a new card. This is why we recommend keeping the card in your passport sleeve from the day you receive it.

Children's vaccinations

Children under 5 should already have their full polio series under Pakistan's EPI schedule. They still need the additional travel booster (OPV or IPV) within the 28-day to 12-month window before Saudi travel. The same yellow card applies.

Other vaccines to consider

While polio is the only one strictly enforced for all Pakistani travellers, Saudi also requires:

  • Meningococcal ACWY: Required for ALL Hajj and Umrah pilgrims globally (not just Pakistanis). Valid for 3 years. NOT free — PKR 4,000-6,500 at private hospitals.
  • Seasonal flu vaccine: Recommended but not mandatory.
  • Yellow fever: Only required if you've recently visited a yellow-fever endemic country.

Al Bari Travel coordinates vaccination scheduling as part of our standard Umrah and Hajj support. We give every pilgrim a printable vaccination timeline 60+ days before departure so the polio booster timing works correctly.

pageFaqs.q: Is the polio vaccine really free at government EPI centres?
pageFaqs.a: Yes — 100% free for all Pakistani citizens. You don't need any kind of medical card or referral. Walk in with your CNIC and passport during clinic hours, get vaccinated, get the yellow card.

pageFaqs.q: Can I get the polio booster at a private hospital instead?
pageFaqs.a: Yes, but it costs PKR 500-1,500 at private hospitals (Aga Khan, Doctors Hospital, Hameed Latif, South City, Shifa). The vaccine and yellow card are identical — only the convenience and cost differ. Saudi immigration accepts both.

pageFaqs.q: I got vaccinated 13 months ago. Is that still valid for Saudi?
pageFaqs.a: No. The 12-month rule is strict. You need a fresh booster. Visit any EPI centre at least 28 days before your Saudi flight.

pageFaqs.q: My yellow card got wet and the print is faded. Will Saudi immigration accept it?
pageFaqs.a: Probably not — if the date, name, or stamp are illegible, get a fresh booster and new card. Don't risk being turned back at Jeddah airport. The replacement booster is free and the cost saved on potential delay is worth it.

pageFaqs.q: Do I need the polio booster every time I visit Saudi?
pageFaqs.a: Effectively yes — because the 12-month validity window means most pilgrims get a fresh booster before each major Umrah / Hajj trip. If you travel back to Saudi within 12 months of your last booster, the original card is still valid.

pageFaqs.q: Can I get the polio booster after arriving in Saudi Arabia?
pageFaqs.a: No — the booster needs to be administered AT LEAST 28 days before arrival in Saudi to be valid for immigration purposes. If you arrive without proof, Saudi immigration may deny entry or quarantine you. Get the booster in Pakistan well in advance.

This is the printable Umrah packing list we hand to every Pakistani pilgrim before they depart. It is built from what our own group leaders carry on every Umrah trip — refined over hundreds of pilgrim journeys. Print it, pin it to your fridge, tick off as you pack.

Documents (carry-on only, never check)

  • Original Machine-Readable Passport (6+ months validity)
  • Printed Saudi e-Visa (A4 paper copy — even though it's electronic)
  • Yellow polio + meningococcal vaccination cards
  • Hotel vouchers (Makkah AND Madinah)
  • Return flight ticket printout
  • 2 passport-size photos (white background, 4×6 cm)
  • CNIC (front + back photocopies)
  • Photocopies of all of the above — kept in a separate bag
  • Travel insurance card (if applicable)
  • Emergency contact list on paper (in case phone dies)

Men's Ihram and clothing

  • 2 sets of Ihram cloth (one to wear, one spare)
  • Ihram belt with zipped pocket for documents
  • Plastic Ihram slippers (no stitching across the top)
  • Pin-free fasteners
  • Casual loose cotton or linen for after Umrah (3-4 sets)
  • One warm layer for Madinah evenings (December-February)
  • Socks for prayer halls
  • Comfortable closed-toe walking shoes (not for Ihram)

Women's clothing

  • 3-4 loose abayas in breathable cotton
  • Prayer scarves (at least 2)
  • Comfortable closed-toe walking shoes
  • Underclothes for hot weather (cotton)
  • One warm layer for Madinah
  • Personal toiletries / hygiene supplies for full duration

Toiletries (unscented during Ihram, scented after)

  • Unscented soap (Dove sensitive / Sebamed)
  • Unscented toothpaste (Sensodyne Original / Colgate Total Original)
  • Unscented shampoo (sachet form to save weight)
  • Toothbrush, miswak, dental floss
  • Nail clippers (use BEFORE Ihram and AFTER — not during)
  • Vaseline (for cracked lips and feet)
  • Wet wipes — non-alcoholic, unscented
  • Sunscreen SPF 50+ (odorless types only during Ihram)
  • Personal feminine hygiene items (sufficient stock)

Medicine kit

  • Personal prescription medicines (original packaging + doctor's note)
  • Panadol / Paracetamol
  • Strepsils / lozenges (sore throat is the #1 complaint)
  • Imodium (anti-diarrhoea)
  • ORS oral rehydration sachets
  • Plasters and blister patches (Compeed-style)
  • Antiseptic cream
  • Surgical or N95 masks (for crowded Tawaf)
  • Multivitamin (basic)

Electronics

  • Mobile phone (unlocked, ready for Saudi SIM)
  • Charger and cable
  • Power bank (10,000 mAh maximum for carry-on)
  • Universal travel adapter (Saudi uses Type G UK 3-pin)
  • Headphones (for Qur'an / dua audio during downtime)
  • Small waterproof zip-pouch for phone (ZamZam splashes)

Money

  • SAR 1,500-2,500 cash per person (for 14-day Umrah)
  • One debit card (Mada / Visa / Mastercard) — confirm international use with bank before flight
  • One backup card stored separately
  • Small SAR notes (5, 10, 20) for tips and street food

Spiritual items

  • Pocket Qur'an or Qur'an app on phone
  • Dua book in Urdu / English
  • Tasbeeh (digital or beaded)
  • Prayer mat (small, foldable)

Small bag for Haram

  • Small zipped sling pouch (for phone, ID, cash, prayer beads inside the Haram)
  • Hand sanitiser (non-alcoholic if during Ihram)
  • Reusable water bottle (refill at ZamZam dispensers)

What NOT to pack

  • Alcohol of any kind (including alcohol-based mouthwash — pack Listerine Zero)
  • Pork products or anything containing pork derivatives
  • Drones, walkie-talkies, large quantities of vapes
  • Religious items considered idolatrous
  • Cash exceeding SAR 60,000 equivalent undeclared
  • Large quantities of medicines beyond personal use without prescription

Final 24-hour checklist

  • Cut nails and trim hair the night before (Sunnah for Ihram preparation)
  • Shower with unscented soap before departure
  • Confirm Ihram is packed and easily accessible
  • Verify e-Visa printout is in carry-on (NOT checked luggage)
  • Save group leader's WhatsApp on phone
  • Download Nusuk, Tawakkalna, Google Maps offline maps of Makkah + Madinah
  • Photograph all documents and email to yourself as backup
  • Confirm Saudi SIM plan or international roaming
  • Set out-of-office email replies
  • Arrange home / pet / business cover for travel duration

This printable list is intentionally text-only so it prints cleanly on one sheet of A4. For a more detailed walk-through with explanations, see our complete Umrah packing guide on the blog.

pageFaqs.q: How much weight can I bring on a Pakistan-Saudi flight?
pageFaqs.a: 30 kg checked + 7 kg cabin on Economy is standard for PIA, Saudia, Air Sial, SereneAir, Emirates, Qatar, and Etihad. FlyJinnah base fare is 20 kg checked. Business class is typically 40 kg. Confirm with your airline at booking.

pageFaqs.q: Can I pack ZamZam water in my luggage?
pageFaqs.a: No. Saudi customs and most airlines prohibit passenger-packed ZamZam. PIA and Saudia provide a free 5L sealed ZamZam allowance at Jeddah Airport's dedicated ZamZam counter after immigration. Use that.

pageFaqs.q: Do I need to buy Ihram in Pakistan or in Saudi?
pageFaqs.a: Buy at least one set in Pakistan (most airports have Ihram shops in international departure). You can also buy in Saudi from any souq for SAR 30-80. Bring one set, buy a spare in Makkah if needed.

pageFaqs.q: Can I bring my own food snacks?
pageFaqs.a: Yes — sealed, non-perishable snacks (biscuits, dates, dry fruit, namkeen) are permitted. Open or homemade food may be confiscated at Saudi customs.

pageFaqs.q: Should I print this checklist or use it on my phone?
pageFaqs.a: Print it. The day before departure when you're actually packing, your phone is usually charging and inconvenient to keep checking. A printed list pinned to the fridge or a wall is how our group leaders do it.

forms.pageBody:
The Saudi Umrah visa application is straightforward when you have every document ready. It is a nightmare when even one item is missing or incorrect. This checklist covers every document required for Pakistani applicants in 2026, across both the traditional Pakistani agent route and the direct Nusuk Masar e-Visa route.

The 8 core documents required

1. Original Machine-Readable Passport (MRP)

Validity at least 6 months beyond your scheduled exit from Saudi Arabia. If yours is borderline, renew at any DGI&P Passport Office BEFORE applying. MRP and e-Passport both accepted; non-MRP old passports are NOT accepted.

2. Passport-size photograph (2 copies)

  • 4 cm wide x 6 cm tall
  • White background, plain
  • Recent (within 6 months)
  • Face fully visible, no smiling, no head turned
  • Men: no head covering. Women: hijab acceptable, face must be visible
  • No glasses (especially tinted)

3. Polio vaccination yellow card

Mandatory for all Pakistani travellers. Must be administered 28 days to 12 months before Saudi arrival. Free at any government EPI centre. Full polio guide here.

4. Meningococcal ACWY vaccination certificate

Required for all Umrah and Hajj pilgrims globally. Valid for 3 years. NOT free — PKR 4,000-6,500 at private hospitals (Aga Khan, Doctors Hospital, Hameed Latif, etc).

5. Confirmed hotel booking in Makkah

Required: hotel name, address, dates of stay, booking confirmation number. Many Pakistani Umrah packages include this. If self-booking via Nusuk Masar, use Booking.com or Almosafer for confirmation.

6. Confirmed hotel booking in Madinah

Same as Makkah — need name, address, dates, confirmation number. If staying in Makkah only, you can skip this; if visiting Madinah at any point during Umrah trip, hotel proof is needed.

7. Confirmed return air ticket

Round-trip air ticket booking confirmation. Saudi authorities want assurance you will leave the country by the visa expiry. Single-leg tickets are sometimes rejected.

8. CNIC (front and back photocopies)

Required. NICOP for overseas Pakistanis. Original CNIC also presented at the Pakistani agent office or VFS centre.

Additional documents (depending on circumstances)

  • For women under 45: Mahram affidavit + NADRA Computerised Marriage Certificate / FRC / B-Form proving relationship. Mahram affidavit guide.
  • For minors (under 18): NADRA computerised birth certificate, both parents' CNIC, and (if travelling without both parents) notarised No-Objection Certificate (NOC) from the absent parent.
  • For Nusuk Masar applications: Bank statement from last 3 months (showing financial capacity).
  • For first-time travellers: Some agents request additional verification — employer NOC or university enrollment letter.

Common reasons applications are rejected

  1. Passport validity less than 6 months (most common rejection)
  2. Photograph not meeting MoFA specifications (wrong background, glasses, smiling)
  3. Previous Saudi visa overstay (results in 3-year ban + SAR 25,000 fine)
  4. Polio vaccination outside 28-day to 12-month window
  5. Conflicting dates between hotel and ticket (e.g. ticket returns 3rd, hotel booked until 5th)
  6. Applying during Hajj-season blackout (mid-Shawwal to mid-Dhu al-Hijjah)
  7. Mahram documentation incomplete (affidavit without supporting NADRA document)
  8. Forged or altered documents — permanent blacklisting

Hajj-season blackout (CRITICAL TIMING)

Saudi MoFA suspends Umrah visa issuance from approximately Shawwal 15 to Dhu al-Hijjah 15 each Hijri year (roughly mid-May to mid-July in 2026-2027). During this window, only confirmed Hajj pilgrims can enter Saudi. Pakistani applicants planning Umrah for May or June should apply early or postpone.

pageFaqs.q: How fast can I get a Saudi Umrah visa from Pakistan?
pageFaqs.a: Fastest is Nusuk Masar e-Visa: 24-72 hours processing if all documents are in order. Pakistani agent route via MoFA: 5-14 days. Saudi Tourist e-Visa via Pakistani embassy: 1-5 days.

pageFaqs.q: Can I apply for a Saudi Umrah visa without using a Pakistani agent?
pageFaqs.a: Yes. Direct application via Nusuk Masar (nusuk.sa) is fully available for Pakistani nationals since 2023. You upload documents online, pay SAR 535 inclusive fee, and receive the e-Visa via email in 24-72 hours.

pageFaqs.q: What happens if my Saudi visa expires while I am in Saudi?
pageFaqs.a: 3-year ban from any Saudi visa, SAR 25,000 fine, and potential deportation. Always exit before stamped expiry. For emergencies (illness, family death), contact the Pakistani Embassy in Riyadh or Consulate in Jeddah immediately.

pageFaqs.q: Do children need separate Saudi visas?
pageFaqs.a: Yes. Every traveller, including infants, needs an individual Saudi visa. Children CAN be added to a parent's application file (one combined application), but each child gets a separate visa with their own visa number.

pageFaqs.q: Can I get an Umrah visa for someone who has been to Israel?
pageFaqs.a: Saudi authorities scrutinise applications from passports showing Israeli entry/exit stamps. Approval is at MoFA discretion. Always disclose travel history honestly — hiding it can result in permanent blacklisting if discovered.

pageFaqs.q: My passport photograph was rejected — what do I do?
pageFaqs.a: Get a new photograph at any professional photo studio (specify "Saudi visa photo" — they know the spec). White background, plain wall behind, no glasses, no head covering for men, hijab OK for women with face fully visible, no smiling, no head turned. Cost in Pakistan: PKR 200-500 for 6-8 prints.

forms.pageSeoDescription: Complete Saudi document attestation guide for Pakistanis — three-stage chain (HEC → MoFA → Saudi Embassy), fees, timeline, common pitfalls, agent vs DIY.
forms.pageBody:
If you are applying for a Saudi work visa, family residence visa, or student visa, your Pakistani documents (degrees, marriage certificates, birth certificates, police clearance) must be attested through a strict three-stage chain. Get the order wrong, miss a stage, or use the wrong office and the entire process starts again. This guide walks through every step in detail.

Why attestation is required

A Pakistani-issued document — a university degree, a marriage certificate, a birth certificate — has no automatic legal force outside Pakistan. The attestation chain serves as official verification at three levels: (1) the document is genuine; (2) the original authority that signed it is recognised by the Pakistani government; (3) Saudi Arabia recognises that Pakistani government recognition.

The three-stage chain (in strict order)

Stage 1: Originating authority attestation

The body that originally issued the document verifies its authenticity. Different documents go through different stage-1 offices:

  • Degrees (BA / BSc / MA / MSc / MBBS / PhD): Higher Education Commission (HEC). Visit your nearest HEC Regional Centre (Islamabad, Lahore, Karachi, Peshawar, Quetta) or apply online via HEC portal. Required: original degree, transcript, CNIC copy, photograph. Processing: 1-7 working days. Fee: PKR 800-1,200 per document.
  • Marriage certificates: NADRA Computerised Marriage Certificate (NOT the original Nikah-nama). Apply at any NADRA Mega Centre. Required: original Nikah-nama, both spouses' CNIC, two witnesses' CNIC. Processing: 7-14 days. Fee: PKR 250-500.
  • Birth certificates: NADRA Computerised Birth Certificate. Apply at NADRA. Required: child's B-Form, both parents' CNIC. Processing: 7-14 days. Fee: PKR 250.
  • Police Clearance Certificate (PCC): District Police Office (DPO) at your home district. Required: CNIC, application form, photograph, sometimes character certificate from local councillor. Processing: 15-30 days. Fee: PKR 200-500.
  • Experience certificates: Original employer attestation (HR seal + signature).

Stage 2: Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA) attestation

MoFA verifies that the originating authority's seal in Stage 1 is legitimate. Visit MoFA Camp Office in:

  • Islamabad (G-5 Foreign Office)
  • Lahore
  • Karachi
  • Peshawar

Required: Stage 1-attested original document. Processing: 1 working day. Fee: PKR 500 per document.

Stage 3: Saudi Embassy / Consulate attestation

Saudi authorities verify that the MoFA attestation in Stage 2 is legitimate. Visit:

  • Saudi Embassy Islamabad (G-5 Diplomatic Enclave) — for Punjab, KP, ICT, AJK, Gilgit-Baltistan residents
  • Saudi Consulate Karachi (Clifton) — for Sindh and Balochistan residents

Required: MoFA-attested original document, photocopy of CNIC, passport copy. Processing: 2-5 working days. Fee: SAR 60 per document (~PKR 4,400 in 2026).

Total cost and time (typical Pakistani worker)

A typical Pakistani heading to Saudi for work needs 3 documents attested: degree, marriage certificate (if going with family), and PCC.

Stage3 Documents
Originating authority (HEC + NADRA + Police)PKR 2,000-3,000
MoFA (3 documents x PKR 500)PKR 1,500
Saudi Embassy (3 documents x PKR 4,400)PKR 13,200
Total (DIY)PKR 16,700-17,700
Total via attestation agentPKR 22,000-32,000

Realistic timeline DIY: 4-8 weeks. With an agent: 3-5 weeks.

Common pitfalls

  • Skipping HEC: MoFA refuses to attest unattested degrees. The chain must go HEC → MoFA → Saudi.
  • Submitting photocopies for embassy attestation: The Saudi Embassy only attests originals.
  • Wrong document type: Saudi requires NADRA Computerised Marriage Certificate, NOT the original Nikah-nama.
  • Document damage: Folded, stapled, or laminated documents are often rejected. Bring documents flat in a folder.
  • Wrong embassy: The Saudi Consulate in Karachi only serves Sindh / Balochistan-resident applicants.
  • Old PCC: PCCs are typically accepted by Saudi authorities for only 6 months from issuance.

The apostille question

Pakistan is NOT a signatory to the Hague Apostille Convention. This means apostille is not available for Pakistani documents — the three-stage chain is mandatory. Documents from Hague-signatory countries (UK, US, EU) need only an apostille; Pakistani documents always need full attestation.

DIY or agent?

For 1-2 documents, DIY is straightforward and saves PKR 10,000-20,000. For 4+ documents (a family with multiple educational degrees + marriage cert + birth certs + PCC), an agent saves significant time. Reputable Rawalpindi and Karachi attestation agents handle hundreds of files monthly. Always verify: their physical office, prior client references, and whether they take possession of your originals (most do — make 2 sets of photocopies before handing over).

pageFaqs.q: How long does Saudi document attestation take in Pakistan?
pageFaqs.a: Typical end-to-end is 4-8 weeks DIY. HEC stage is slowest (1-2 weeks). MoFA is 1 day. Saudi Embassy 2-5 days. Bottleneck is usually originating-authority issuance (NADRA marriage 2 weeks, PCC 15-30 days).

pageFaqs.q: Can I attest Pakistani documents from outside Pakistan?
pageFaqs.a: No. Pakistani documents must be attested in Pakistan via HEC/NADRA/Police + MoFA + Saudi Embassy. Pakistani embassies abroad cannot perform this chain. Most expats use a trusted family member or attestation agent in Pakistan.

pageFaqs.q: Does Saudi accept Pakistani degrees without HEC attestation?
pageFaqs.a: No. Saudi work visa and student visa applications strictly require HEC-attested degrees. Without it, MoFA refuses to attest, breaking the chain.

pageFaqs.q: Is the Saudi Consulate Karachi or Embassy Islamabad better?
pageFaqs.a: It depends on your residence per CNIC. Karachi Consulate serves Sindh and Balochistan. Islamabad Embassy serves Punjab, KP, ICT, AJK, GB. Both produce identical attestation.

pageFaqs.q: Can I use a courier service to send my documents to Saudi Embassy Islamabad?
pageFaqs.a: The Saudi Embassy typically requires in-person submission. Reputable attestation agents act as your in-person representative if you cannot travel to Islamabad yourself.

forms.pageSeoDescription: Editable Schengen visa cover letter template for Pakistani applicants — covers travel purpose, financial commitment, ties to Pakistan, return intent.
forms.pageBody:
The cover letter is one of the most underrated documents in a Schengen visa application. Pakistani applicants who skip it or submit a generic template often face rejection. A strong cover letter addresses each consular concern directly, references your supporting evidence, and demonstrates clear intent to return to Pakistan. This page provides a customisable template and explains exactly what to include.

What a Schengen cover letter must achieve

  1. Establish travel purpose — tourism, family visit, business meeting, conference attendance
  2. Confirm specific itinerary — cities, dates, accommodation, return flight
  3. Demonstrate financial capacity — reference your bank statements, employment, source of funds
  4. Establish strong ties to Pakistan — the most critical element for Pakistani applicants (employment, family, property, ongoing studies, business obligations)
  5. Confirm intent to return — explicitly state return plan with date
  6. Reference all supporting documents by name

Template (customise the highlighted sections)

[Your full name as on passport]
[Your CNIC number]
[Your home address in Pakistan]
[Your contact email and phone number]
[Today's date]

The Consul General
[Consulate name — e.g. Embassy of France in Islamabad]
[Address]

Subject: Schengen Visa Application — [Your name] — [Passport number]

Dear Sir / Madam,

I am writing in support of my Schengen visa application to visit [country/countries] from [departure date] to [return date], with the purpose of [tourism / family visit / business meeting / conference].

Travel itinerary:

  • [Date]: Arrival in [city], staying at [hotel name]
  • [Date]: Visit to [city/attraction]
  • [Date]: Travel to [next city] for [purpose]
  • [Date]: Departure from [city] returning to [Pakistan city]

Financial responsibility: I will fully fund this trip myself / my [relationship] is sponsoring this trip. My bank account at [Pakistani bank name] holds [PKR amount] as shown in the attached 6-month bank statement (Document 4 in the file). Estimated trip cost is approximately EUR [amount], covered by these funds plus my current employment salary of PKR [monthly salary] per month at [employer name] (Document 5).

Ties to Pakistan: I am [a permanent employee at / business owner of / a registered student at] [organisation name] since [start date] (employment letter / business registration attached as Document 6). My spouse [name] and our [number] children [names + ages] reside with me at the address above (NADRA family documents attached as Document 7). I own [property type] in [city] (property documents attached as Document 8). I have ongoing financial commitments to [insurance / loan / school fees] in Pakistan.

Return intent: I will return to Pakistan on [date] via [airline name, flight number] to resume my work at [employer] / studies at [institution] / family responsibilities. My confirmed return flight booking is attached.

Previous international travel: [List previous visits with year and country — helps establish travel pattern. If first-time international, omit this paragraph or say "This will be my first international trip; I have a clean passport with no prior overstay or rejection."]

Travel insurance: Comprehensive travel insurance covering EUR 30,000 across the Schengen Area for the full trip duration has been purchased from [insurance provider] (Document 9).

All documents listed are attached to this application. I am happy to provide any additional information requested.

Thank you for considering my application.

Sincerely,
[Signature]
[Your full name typed]

Key tips for Pakistani applicants

  • Be specific. "Sightseeing in Europe" is weak. "Visit the Eiffel Tower 12 Aug, Louvre 13 Aug, day-trip to Versailles 14 Aug" is strong.
  • Reference document numbers. Consular officers process applications in batches; they appreciate cover letters that point to specific evidence in the file.
  • One page maximum. Concise wins. If your cover letter spills onto page two, tighten it.
  • English is preferred. All Schengen embassies accept English. Don't submit Urdu unless required.
  • Sign in pen. Print, sign with a real pen, then scan if uploading.
  • Don't over-promise. If you say you'll return on a specific flight, make sure you actually have that booking.
  • Match the consulate's tone. French consulate is more formal than Spanish; German is the most formal.

What NOT to include

  • Emotional appeals or stories of personal hardship
  • Promises you cannot back up
  • Negative comments about previous visa rejections
  • Mention of intent to extend the stay or apply for residence
  • Mention of intent to work abroad

Al Bari Travel routinely prepares Schengen cover letters for Pakistani applicants as part of our visit visa service. WhatsApp +92 315 9596161 for a free consultation.

pageFaqs.q: Is a Schengen cover letter mandatory?
pageFaqs.a: Not technically mandatory but strongly recommended, especially for Pakistani applicants who face higher rejection rates (~32% at most consulates in 2024). A well-written cover letter directly addresses consular concerns and significantly improves approval odds.

pageFaqs.q: Can I use the same cover letter for different Schengen countries?
pageFaqs.a: Apply at the embassy of the country where you'll spend the most days. The cover letter should be addressed to that specific consulate and reference its country as your primary destination, even if you're visiting multiple Schengen countries.

pageFaqs.q: How long should the cover letter be?
pageFaqs.a: One page (A4) maximum. Consular officers process thousands of applications — tight, specific letters get read carefully. Long rambling letters get skimmed.

pageFaqs.q: Should the cover letter be on company letterhead if I am employed?
pageFaqs.a: No — the cover letter is from YOU personally. Your employer NOC (separate document) is on company letterhead. The cover letter is on plain paper or your own personal letterhead.

pageFaqs.q: Do I need to print the cover letter in colour?
pageFaqs.a: Black-and-white print is fine. What matters is content and clarity, not visual presentation.

pageFaqs.q: Can someone else write the cover letter for me?
pageFaqs.a: Anyone can draft it, but it must be signed by you personally and must reflect your circumstances accurately. Consular interviews sometimes test whether you actually understand what you submitted.

forms.pageBody:
The UK Student Visa (formerly Tier 4) is one of the most-applied-for visas by Pakistani students — over 14,000 granted in 2024. The application is well-defined but unforgiving: one missing document or one financial-evidence mistake and the visa is refused. This checklist covers every document required for Pakistani applicants in 2026.

Pre-application requirements

  1. Unconditional offer from a UK university or college that holds a Student Sponsor Licence (verify at gov.uk register of licensed sponsors)
  2. Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS) — 14-digit reference issued by your sponsor via UK Home Office system after you accept the offer and pay any required deposit
  3. English language requirement met via IELTS Academic, Pearson PTE, TOEFL iBT, or equivalent SELT
  4. Funds in place — held in your account for 28 consecutive days before application

Core documents for visa application

1. Passport

  • Original Machine-Readable Pakistani Passport
  • Valid for the whole duration of the visa + 1 month
  • At least one blank page for the visa vignette

2. CAS letter

  • Printed PDF copy of the CAS letter from your sponsor
  • CAS reference number is what UK Home Office actually uses; the printed letter is supporting evidence

3. Financial evidence

The most common rejection ground. UK requires:

  • First-year tuition (varies by course — typically GBP 15,000-35,000 for international students)
  • Living costs: GBP 1,483/month for London for 9 months max (= GBP 13,347) OR GBP 1,136/month outside London for 9 months max (= GBP 10,224)
  • Funds held for 28 consecutive days in your name (or parent's name with affidavit of support)
  • Bank statement no older than 31 days at submission
  • Statement must show: account holder name, account number, bank name, daily closing balances showing 28-day hold

Acceptable sources: Pakistani bank statement, regulated student loan letter, parent's bank statement (with affidavit of support), recognised scholarship letter.

4. English language certificate

  • IELTS Academic, Pearson PTE, TOEFL iBT, Trinity GESE/ISE, LanguageCert (must be from UKVI-approved SELT centre)
  • Score requirements vary by course; minimum typically IELTS 6.0 overall with no band below 5.5 for degree-level
  • Some Pakistani A-Level grade C+ in English Language may be accepted by sponsors

5. Academic transcripts

  • Original transcripts from previous qualifications
  • Required even after CAS issuance for verification

6. Polio vaccination certificate

  • Mandatory for all Pakistani applicants entering the UK from 2024
  • Free at any government EPI centre in Pakistan
  • Yellow card carried with passport

7. TB test certificate from IOM

  • Pakistani applicants MUST complete TB testing at an IOM (International Organization for Migration) approved centre in Pakistan
  • IOM centres: Karachi (Defence), Islamabad (F-7), Lahore (Gulberg)
  • Cost: ~USD 75 (PKR 21,000)
  • Certificate valid 6 months from issuance

8. Parent / sponsor affidavit

If using parent's funds, notarised affidavit of support stating the parent will fund your studies, plus their CNIC copy and proof of relationship (NADRA FRC or B-Form).

9. Biometric appointment booking

Book at VFS Karachi (Clifton), VFS Islamabad (Blue Area), or VFS Lahore via online application.

Fees (2026)

FeeAmount
Visa application feeGBP 524 (~PKR 196,000)
Immigration Health Surcharge (IHS)GBP 776 per year of course
For a 3-year UG degree, IHS total~GBP 2,328 (~PKR 870,000)
Standard processing~3 weeks
Priority service (5 working days)+ GBP 500
Super Priority (1 working day)+ GBP 1,000

Common reasons applications are refused

  1. Financial evidence not held for 28 consecutive days — even one day dipping below the threshold restarts the clock
  2. Bank statement older than 31 days at submission
  3. Discrepancy between sponsor records and visa application (course name, intake date)
  4. Credibility interview failure — UKVI sometimes calls applicants; inability to explain why this course / university / city is a common rejection
  5. Forged or altered documents — instant 10-year ban
  6. Prior UK visa refusal not declared
  7. Missing TB test certificate
  8. Polio vaccination card missing

2024 reform: dependants restriction

Since January 2024, UK Student Visa holders can NO LONGER bring dependants (spouse, children) UNLESS pursuing a PhD or government-sponsored research course of 9+ months. This significantly affects taught Master's students with families.

After arrival in the UK

  • Pick up Biometric Residence Permit (BRP) within 10 days of arrival
  • Register with police if required (rare for student visas)
  • Work limit: 20 hours/week during term-time, full-time during vacation, IF on degree-level course at tracked HEI
  • Apply for Graduate Route within 2 months of finishing degree — 2 years stay (UG/Master's) or 3 years (PhD)

Al Bari Travel coordinates UK Student Visa applications for Pakistani students from initial offer guidance through BRP collection. WhatsApp +92 315 9596161 for free consultation.

pageFaqs.q: How much money do I need to show for a UK Student Visa?
pageFaqs.a: First-year tuition + 9 months living costs (GBP 13,347 outside London / GBP 17,796 in London). Funds held 28 consecutive days, bank statement no older than 31 days at submission. For typical London Master's, expect to show GBP 50,000+ in evidence.

pageFaqs.q: How long does UK Student Visa take from Pakistan?
pageFaqs.a: Standard: ~3 weeks. Priority (GBP 500 extra): 5 working days. Super Priority (GBP 1,000 extra): 1 working day.

pageFaqs.q: Can I bring my family on UK Student Visa from Pakistan?
pageFaqs.a: Only if pursuing PhD or government-sponsored programme of 9+ months. Since January 2024, taught Master's and undergraduate students cannot bring dependants.

pageFaqs.q: Can I work during UK studies?
pageFaqs.a: 20 hours per week during term time, full-time during vacation, IF enrolled in degree-level course at tracked Higher Education Provider. Below-degree level has no work rights.

pageFaqs.q: What is the Graduate Route after I finish?
pageFaqs.a: Post-Study Work Visa allowing 2 years stay (UG/Master's) or 3 years (PhD) without job sponsor. Apply within 2 months of degree completion.

forms.pageSeoTitle: UK Visitor Visa Pakistan 2026 — Documents & Process
forms.pageSeoDescription: UK Standard Visitor Visa checklist for Pakistani applicants — required documents, financial evidence, sponsor letter, ties to Pakistan, VFS submission.
forms.pageBody:
The UK Standard Visitor Visa lets a Pakistani national visit the UK for tourism, family visit, business meetings, short-term study, or medical treatment for up to 6 months. Pakistani applications face moderate-to-high rejection rates — strong documentation and clear ties to Pakistan are essential. This guide covers everything needed.

What the Standard Visitor Visa permits

  • Tourism (sightseeing, shopping, attractions)
  • Visit family or friends
  • Business meetings, conferences, training
  • Short courses lasting under 6 months
  • Medical treatment (private)
  • Recreational activities (cricket matches, weddings, religious events)

What it does NOT permit

  • Working (paid or unpaid except specific business activities)
  • Studying at school or accredited courses over 6 months
  • Accessing public funds (NHS for medical issues unrelated to your visit)
  • Living in the UK through frequent or successive visits

Required documents

1. Passport

  • Original MRP/e-Passport valid for whole intended trip
  • At least one blank page

2. Confirmed return travel

  • Return flight booking confirmation
  • UK accommodation: hotel booking, Airbnb, or invitation letter from UK-based host

3. Financial evidence

  • Last 6 months of Pakistani bank statements (bank-stamped)
  • Salary slips (last 3 months) if employed
  • Tax returns / FBR NTN certificate
  • Property documents (if any)
  • Approximate guideline: enough funds to cover the trip + GBP 50-80 per day living costs + return home

4. Employment proof

  • NOC from employer on company letterhead stating leave dates, position, salary, and confirmed return to post
  • For business owners: company registration, recent business bank statement, FBR documents
  • For students: enrollment certificate + parent affidavit

5. Travel history

  • Photocopies of pages showing previous visa stamps (Saudi, UAE, Schengen, etc.)
  • Establishes you have a pattern of legal international travel and return

6. Family ties documentation

  • NADRA Computerised Marriage Certificate (if married)
  • Children's NADRA birth certificates (if you have children)
  • Establishes you have responsibilities pulling you home

7. UK sponsor invitation (if visiting family)

  • Letter from UK-based family / friend inviting you
  • Their UK immigration status (citizen/ILR/visa copy)
  • Their UK address proof (utility bill or council tax)
  • Their financial capacity to host you (if they're sponsoring your accommodation/expenses)
  • NADRA proof of relationship to UK sponsor (if family)

8. Polio + meningococcal vaccination cards

Polio mandatory for all Pakistanis entering UK from 2024. Meningococcal recommended.

9. TB test certificate

Required for stays over 6 months but recommended for all Pakistani applicants. IOM Karachi / Islamabad / Lahore.

Application process

  1. Apply online at gov.uk — select "Standard Visitor Visa"
  2. Pay visa fee GBP 127 for up to 6 months
  3. Book biometric appointment at VFS Karachi, Lahore, or Islamabad
  4. Attend biometric appointment with all original documents
  5. Wait 15 working days for standard processing (Priority and Super Priority available for extra fees)
  6. Collect passport with visa from VFS or have it couriered

Fees (2026)

ServiceFee
Standard Visitor Visa (6 months)GBP 127
Long-term (2 years)GBP 475
Long-term (5 years)GBP 848
Long-term (10 years)GBP 1,059
Priority service+ GBP 500
Super Priority+ GBP 1,000

Why Pakistani applications get refused

  1. Weak ties to Pakistan — the #1 reason. Single young applicants without family / employment / property face the most scrutiny.
  2. Inconsistent bank activity — large unexplained deposits just before application
  3. Unrealistic travel purpose — vague answers like "just visiting" without concrete plans
  4. UK sponsor whose own status is shaky — recent visa, unstable employment
  5. Previous overstay or visa refusal — major red flag
  6. Forged documents — instant 10-year ban

How to strengthen a Pakistani application

  • 6 months of consistent bank activity matching your stated income
  • Strong employment letter on company letterhead with HR contact
  • Property documents, business registration, family responsibilities all documented
  • Specific itinerary with named hotels and attractions
  • Refundable hotel bookings (Booking.com free cancellation)
  • Prior travel history to Saudi, UAE, Schengen, Turkey, Malaysia, Thailand — shows pattern of legal travel
  • Cover letter framing trip purpose and return intent

Al Bari Travel prepares UK Visitor Visa files for Pakistani applicants as part of our visit visa service. WhatsApp +92 315 9596161 for free consultation.

pageFaqs.q: How long does UK Visitor Visa take from Pakistan?
pageFaqs.a: Standard processing: 15 working days. Priority service (GBP 500 extra): 5 working days. Super Priority (GBP 1,000 extra): 24 hours.

pageFaqs.q: Can I stay in the UK longer than 6 months on a visit visa?
pageFaqs.a: No. Standard Visitor Visa is strictly 6 months maximum per visit. Long-term multi-entry visas (2/5/10 years) allow multiple 6-month visits but each individual visit cannot exceed 6 months.

pageFaqs.q: Can I get medical treatment in the UK on visit visa?
pageFaqs.a: Yes for private medical treatment (you pay full cost). NHS treatment requires separate arrangements. Specify medical purpose at application and provide doctor referral, treatment plan, and proof of funds.

pageFaqs.q: Does invitation from a UK family member guarantee approval?
pageFaqs.a: No. UK invitations help but the consular officer assesses YOUR ties to Pakistan, your financial capacity, and your travel history. A UK invitation supports the case; it does not override weaknesses in your own profile.

pageFaqs.q: Can I extend my visitor visa once I am in the UK?
pageFaqs.a: No, generally not. Standard Visitor Visa cannot be extended in-country. You must leave the UK before the visa expires and apply again from Pakistan for a new visit.

forms.pageSeoDescription: Master Gulf work visa document checklist for Pakistani workers — Saudi, UAE, Qatar, Bahrain, Oman, Kuwait. Attestation, GAMCA, POE Protector, demand letter.
forms.pageBody:
Over 2 million Pakistanis work in the GCC, making Pakistan the largest source country of expatriate labour in the Gulf. The work-visa process is broadly similar across all 6 GCC countries with country-specific variations. This master checklist covers everything needed for Pakistani workers heading to Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, Bahrain, Oman, or Kuwait.

Stage 1: Job offer + employer-side preparation

Before YOUR paperwork starts, the Gulf-side employer must:

  1. Issue a Demand Letter / Offer Letter / Wakala (Saudi term) specifying job, salary, contract duration, accommodation arrangements
  2. Obtain approved visa quota / Block Visa / Labour Approval from their country's Labour Ministry
  3. Submit your details to relevant Gulf authority

Stage 2: Pakistani document attestation

Three-stage attestation chain for each required document:

  • Educational degree (HEC + MoFA + Embassy): For skilled positions — engineers, doctors, IT, finance, hospitality managers, teachers. See full attestation guide.
  • Police Clearance Certificate (PCC) + MoFA + Embassy: Required for most worker visas. PCC issued by District Police Office, usually 15-30 days.
  • Marriage certificate (NADRA + MoFA + Embassy): Required only if bringing family on residence visa. Use the NADRA Computerised Marriage Certificate, NOT the original Nikah-nama.
  • Children's birth certificates (NADRA + MoFA + Embassy): Required only if bringing children on family residence visa.
  • Experience certificates from previous employers: For skilled positions. Original employer attestation + MoFA + Embassy.
  • Profession-specific verifications: Pakistan Medical Commission for doctors, Pakistan Engineering Council for engineers, etc.

Stage 3: GAMCA medical examination

Mandatory for all Gulf work visas. Full GAMCA guide here.

  • Find authorised centre at wafid.com
  • Tests: HIV, Hep B/C, syphilis, TB X-ray, drug screen, pregnancy (women), ECG (over 40)
  • Cost: PKR 6,500-9,500
  • Report turnaround: 2-4 working days
  • Validity: 90 days (60 days for some Gulf countries)

Stage 4: Visa stamping at destination country embassy / consulate

With attested documents + GAMCA fitness + demand letter, apply at:

  • Saudi Embassy Islamabad / Consulate Karachi — for Saudi visas
  • UAE Embassy Islamabad / Consulate Karachi — for UAE visas
  • Qatar Embassy Islamabad / Consulate Karachi — for Qatar visas
  • etc.

Processing: 5-15 working days typical.

Stage 5: POE Protector stamp (MANDATORY)

Before flying, every Pakistani going to the Gulf for work MUST get the Protector stamp at a Bureau of Emigration and Overseas Employment (BEMB) office. POE Protector guide.

  • 8 POE offices: Karachi, Lahore, Islamabad, Multan, Rawalpindi, Peshawar, Quetta, Faisalabad
  • Fee: PKR 1,000
  • Without this stamp, Pakistani airport immigration will block you from boarding the Gulf-bound flight

Country-specific variations

Saudi Arabia

  • ~2.6M Pakistani workers (largest single Gulf destination)
  • Kafala (sponsor) system under reform
  • Iqama (residence permit) issued after arrival
  • SAR 200-800 monthly Iqama fee, sponsor-paid

UAE

  • ~1.7M Pakistani workers
  • 2-month Employment Visa for entry, converted to Residence Visa
  • Tawjeeh orientation (1 day) mandatory for new arrivals
  • Emirates ID issued for residents

Qatar

  • ~200,000 Pakistani workers
  • Hayya app card required since 2022
  • Kafala reformed 2020 — workers can change jobs without sponsor permission

Kuwait, Bahrain, Oman

  • Smaller Pakistani populations
  • Country-specific permit categories
  • Each has its own labour authority

Total cost (Pakistani worker side, 2026)

ItemPKR
3 documents attested (degree + PCC + marriage)20,000-32,000

Typical total120,000-350,000

Critical worker rights to verify before signing

  • Read contract in full BEFORE leaving Pakistan
  • Wage in writing — some employers reduce wages after arrival (illegal but happens)
  • Food and accommodation arrangements
  • Keep contract copy in Pakistan with family
  • Working hours, weekly off, annual leave, return ticket entitlement
  • End-of-service gratuity terms (legally mandated in most Gulf countries)
  • Probation period (usually 90 days)
  • Refuse Arabic-only contracts without notarised translation

Avoiding fraud

Only accept Gulf job offers via licensed channels:

  • OEC (Bureau of Emigration and Overseas Employment Promoters)
  • POE-registered Overseas Employment Promoters — verify license on bemb.gov.pk
  • Direct employer offers from established GCC firms

Unregistered "agents" charging PKR 200,000-500,000 for promised Gulf jobs are a major source of fraud.

pageFaqs.q: How long does the full Gulf work visa process take?
pageFaqs.a: Realistic end-to-end is 8-16 weeks: 2-3 weeks for employer demand letter, 4-6 weeks Pakistani attestation, 1-2 weeks GAMCA medical, 1-3 weeks embassy stamping, 1 week POE Protector + travel.

pageFaqs.q: Can I work in Gulf without using a Pakistani agent?
pageFaqs.a: Yes, if you have a direct job offer from a Gulf employer. Skilled professionals (engineers, doctors, IT, finance) often secure direct offers. Lower-skilled positions typically go through Pakistani Overseas Employment Promoters.

pageFaqs.q: What is the maximum legal fee a Pakistani agent can charge?
pageFaqs.a: Pakistani law caps OEP fees based on job category and destination, typically PKR 50,000-200,000. Agents charging significantly more are violating the law. Always demand a receipt and verify the OEP license on bemb.gov.pk.

pageFaqs.q: Can I bring my family on a Gulf work visa?
pageFaqs.a: Yes in most cases, IF your salary meets the minimum threshold (SAR 3,000+/month Saudi; AED 4,000+/month UAE; QAR 10,000+/month Qatar for white-collar). Lower-paid workers (construction, domestic) usually cannot.

pageFaqs.q: Why is the POE Protector stamp mandatory?
pageFaqs.a: Pakistan Emigration Ordinance requires the Protector stamp to ensure workers are protected by Pakistani labour rights frameworks, can access support if abused abroad, and have a legal record of their overseas employment.
